result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God Medicare Mental Health Service Armadale

We are seeking an enthusiastic and compassionate Administration Officer to join our Medicare Mental Health Service in Armadale on a permanent part-time basis.

As an Administration Officer, you will play an important role in supporting the delivery of a welcoming, accessible, and client-focused service. You will provide high-quality administrative and clerical support to the team, while creating a positive first point of contact for clients, their families, and carers accessing our service. You will also support caregivers with a range of administrative tasks that enable the effective delivery of mental health services.

The Armadale Medicare Mental Health Centre provides free, easily accessible support for people aged 18 years and over. We offer a welcoming and inclusive environment where individuals can access mental health information, services, and support from qualified professionals, without the need for an appointment or referral.

Our service is delivered by dedicated mental health professionals, with clients supported from the moment they arrive by trained peer workers who provide guidance and connection throughout their experience. This is an opportunity to contribute to a service that helps people access the right support at the right time.

The Position

Provide administrative support to the Service Manager and team.

Establish and manage effective and efficient office management systems.

Prioritise and coordinate work to meet designated time frames.

Manage the electronic client management system (CMS) for client records and administrative information.

Assist caregivers with the collection of data for quality indicators, finance reports and service specific statistics.

Support data extraction and analytics for benchmarking.

Provide secretarial support to service meetings.

Ensure typing and distribution of minutes, correspondence and memos are completed in an accurate and timely manner.

Arrange venues, equipment and catering for all service events.

Manage an effective filing system for client records and administrative information, including manual and electronic systems.

Assist in the design and desktop production of presentations, fliers, reports and publications.

You will hold strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build positive relationships and engage effectively with a diverse client base, caregivers, and stakeholders. Whilst providing a welcoming and supportive experience for individuals accessing the service, you will have the ability to respond with professionalism and empathy to their needs.

The successful applicant will have solid experience in reception and office administration, with an understanding of systems and processes used to manage client information, appointments, and data collection. You will demonstrate a high level of customer service, with strong verbal and written communication skills, excellent attention to detail and accurate data entry capabilities.

In addition, you will possess sound planning and organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks, manage competing demands, and work effectively in a busy service environment. 

A current WA driver's licence and National Police Clearance are essential for this role.

Above all, patient care will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

We can offer you

Salary: $74,627 to $78,011 (pro-rata for part-time) plus 12% Superannuation

Permanent part-time, working 20 hours per week

Monday to Friday | 8.30 to 12.30pm

Salary packaging up to $18,550 on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses as well as options to salary package benefits above the FBT cap on items such as:

Novated leasing 

work related expenses

self-education and

additional superannuation

A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options, additional purchased leave & well-being programs

Access to gym membership, fitness and wellbeing benefits through Fitness Passport for you and your family.

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

Employee support through our dedicated free Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Innovative Professional Development opportunities

All applicants are asked to submit a current CV and covering letter (of no more than two (2) pages) demonstrating how you meet the above position requirements.

For enquiries contact Liam Dekker, Manager Medicare Mental Health Service on 0437 020 195.

Applications will be reviewed throughout the advertising period and interviews conducted regularly. If suitable applicants are identified advertisement may close prior to listed date. Apply today!

Our commitment is to create a safe and nurturing environment for all children and vulnerable individuals in our care and proactively take steps to protect them from abuse, ensuring their safety and well-being. 

Our inclusive culture fosters an environment that is respectful and secure, welcoming and accessible, and unified through our diverse community.    Click here to Apply now →

result.description: Yahweh care PTY LTD  Yahweh Care Pty Ltd is seeking a compassionate and dedicated Community Worker to join our growing team and support people living with disability to achieve greater independence, wellbeing and community participation.   Benefits  The remuneration is AU$75,000 - AU$85,000 per annum plus superannuation.   Task & responsibilities   Assessing clients’ individual circumstances, social needs, goals and barriers to participation, and contributing to the development and implementation of support strategies that promote community inclusion, independence and wellbeing.  Observing clients’ circumstances, needs and progress through regular communication and interaction, and providing feedback to assist with the planning and adjustment of support strategies.  Supporting clients to develop practical life skills, confidence and capacity to participate more independently in community, recreational, social, education, health and welfare programs.  Assisting clients to identify, access and engage with appropriate community resources, welfare services, support programs and service providers, including facilitating referrals and supporting attendance where required.  Implementing community-based support strategies and participation activities that encourage clients to build social connections, strengthen personal wellbeing and engage meaningfully with their local community.  Monitoring clients’ wellbeing, behaviour and changing support needs, and reporting concerns, incidents, risks or progress updates to supervisors and relevant support personnel.  Maintaining accurate, timely and confidential progress notes, client records and incident documentation in accordance with organisational policies, NDIS Practice Standards and legislative requirements.  Following individual support plans, organisational procedures, safeguarding practices and workplace health and safety requirements to ensure safe and respectful service delivery.  Liaising with clients, families, carers, colleagues and relevant service providers to support continuity of care and assist clients to access additional services where required.  Providing clients with information about available community resources, welfare services, support programs and participation opportunities.  Building positive, respectful and professional relationships with clients, families, colleagues and community contacts while promoting a culturally inclusive and person-centred support environment.    Qualification & experience  Qualifications   At least a Diploma in Community Services, Disability, Individual Support, Aged Care, or a related field.   Experience   Minimum one year of relevant work experience in disability support, aged care, community care, personal care, or a similar support worker/community worker role.   Skills   Good communication and interpersonal skills.  Caring, patient, and respectful attitude.  Ability to work independently and as part of a team.  Reliability, honesty, and a strong commitment to supporting others.   Other requirements   Current NDIS Worker Screening Check or willingness to obtain.  Current Working With Children Check or willingness to obtain.  Current First Aid and CPR Certificate or willingness to obtain.  Valid driver’s licence and access to a reliable vehicle (not essential but preferred).   About Company     Yahweh Care is a registered NDIS provider committed to delivering quality, person-centred support services across Western Sydney. Our mission is to care with compassion, respect, and integrity while empowering participants to live with confidence and independence.    We are passionate about building inclusive communities where every individual is valued, respected, and supported to achieve their goals. Our team is committed to delivering high-quality services that promote choice, dignity, and meaningful outcomes for the people we support. Where there's life, there's Mercy.
Where there's care, there's You.

Through the battles and the breakthroughs, we're there. Where will you be?

For over a century, our incredible teams have provided care for people when they need it most. Our Home Care team feels great pride in this, and they value the security and stability we offer. But it also means so much opportunity - to build on all that's gone before, to grow your impact and gain experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

As a for-purpose organisation with over 10,000 dedicated, compassionate people, we continue to offer more services and deeper care than ever before. With Mercy, you'll have the chance to make an impact and gain experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

At Mercy Health, it's all about taking what we have and making it better. 

To do that, we need you.

Join us at Mercy Health, and help our teams deliver even greater outcomes. 

About the opportunity
At Mercy Health, each moment, no matter how small, truly matters - and as a Domestic Assistant, you'll create cherished moments each day.

We are currently looking for passionate people to support our Home Care clients to live independently at home by providing domestic assistance with cleaning and laundry duties

Ongoing support provided by a dedicated service team.

Flexible working hours.

Mobile phone.

What you'll bring
You're reliable, resilient and have a whole lot of heart. Most importantly, you are genuinely interested in supporting others and making a difference in your community.

To thrive in this role, you will have:

Certificate III in Home or Aged Care is advantageous, but not essential.

Passion about helping people in your community, with strong relationship building, time management and budget management skills.

Previous case management experience as well as relevant qualifications.

Current Victorian Drivers Licence.

Strong communication and organisational skills.

A safe, sensible approach with a practical understanding of people's physical limitations.

The ability to be flexible and adapt to meet clients' individual needs.

We would also love you to have:

A current NDIS Workers screening check

Ready to help us shape the future of healthcare?

Join us and make a meaningful difference in people's lives - and your career.
